ahmad: quick heads-up — I'm seeing a subtle token misalignment after int8 quant on a Mistral-derived variant. outputs start drifting around ~2k tokens, with repeated fragments and probability collapse.

lina: repro steps?

ahmad: minimal repro: 
```
python -m bench.run --model mistralx-local-int8 --prompt-file samples/long.txt --quant backend=tq
```
logs show: `kv_cache shapes mismatch: k: (12,64,128) v: (12,65,128)` and decoder probs diverge.

matt: can you paste tokenizer mapping? could be merged-token aliasing when we build vocab.bin

ahmad: tokenizer diff (excerpt):
```
# upstream vocab (example)
'▁the': 1452
'Ġthe': 1452
# our local merge (bad):
'the': 1452
```
That aliasing + a rotary-scale mismatch probably shifts positions when the kv index uses tokenids mapped differently.

sophia: two quick checks: 1) verify rotary scaling param (rope_freq / rotary_alpha) matches upstream; 2) run eval with fp16 to confirm quant is the trigger.
Command to run fp16 check:
```
./scripts/eval-runner --model local/mistralx --quant none --prompt-set mt-long 
```

dev-bot: CI job kv-cache-offsets (eng-ml/quant-smoke) failed — see https://ci.redwood/12345/kv-cache-offsets :x:

lina: I'll triage. proposed plan: (a) pin tokenizer generation to upstream commit hash, (b) add explicit rotary_scale field in model config, (c) add unit test asserting kv_cache key/val length equality across tokenization variants.

ahmad: will open PR with tokenizer compare + failing test. tagging @matt for the token-map script.

matt: ack. quick scan: our normalization regex strips leading marker bytes in some languages, collapsing distinct tokens to one id. will update script to preserve marker bytes before dedup.

sophia: also add a nightly eval: mt-bench long-context with int8, fail PR if perplexity regresses >8% vs baseline.

ahmad: thanks all :thumbsup:
